title: AWS Cost Management Tools knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is directly listed as a subtopic of “AWS Cost Management Tools”?
options: A concept outside this lesson's stated scope
A deployment choice that has no relationship to the named AWS topic
A reason to skip identity, testing or cleanup controls
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “AWS Budgets” under lesson 219, “AWS Cost Management Tools”. The other choices are unrelated distractors.

questions.prompt: Which approach best fits “AWS Cost Management Tools” in a safe AWS workflow?
options: Deploy first and check permissions, logs and costs only if something fails.
Assume a successful screen or one run proves availability and security.
Use actual usage data, estimates and metrics to compare cost/performance alternatives.
Use one broad permanent credential and avoid documenting assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Use actual usage data, estimates and metrics to compare cost/performance alternatives.
questions.explanation: Budgets notify; they do not inherently stop all spending.

questions.prompt: A workflow related to “AWS Cost Management Tools” behaves unexpectedly. What is the most useful next step?
options: Assume the service is broken without checking quota, Region, routing or policy context.
Verify prerequisites and the resolved identity/Region, inspect the relevant resource state and logs, then change one variable at a time and retest.
Open all network paths and grant administrator permissions so the error disappears.
Repeat the same action indefinitely without inspecting logs or returned errors.
questions.answer_key: Verify prerequisites and the resolved identity/Region, inspect the relevant resource state and logs, then change one variable at a time and retest.
questions.explanation: Troubleshooting should narrow the cause using prerequisites, identity/Region, resource state, logs and a controlled retest. Broad permissions and blind retries can introduce additional risk.
